doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Debussy and Rachmaninoff as influences, and Oscar Peterson
summary: She calls Debussy her lyricism man and Rachmaninoff her Oscar Peterson, and mentions a coming tribute to Peterson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You also cited Debussy and Rachmaninoff as two of your early influences.

That‘s right. Debussy is my lyricism man, and Rachmaninoff is my Oscar Peterson man. I was in San Francisco and I just got it. I was really thrilled, you know. He wants that I be a part of his tribute.
Right. Yes. It just kind of knocked me out, you know, when I got there. Yes, I‘m really thrilled, because he‘s been my Rachmaninoff all my life, and he‘s a bad motorcycle. [laughs]
